title: Changes in state
competency: Use melting, freezing, evaporation, condensation, sublimation and deposition to describe changes of state.

keywords.def: The change of a substance from one physical form to another.
A solid changes into a liquid on heating. Also called fusion.
A liquid changes into a solid. Also called solidification.
A liquid changes into a gas.
A gas changes into a liquid.
A solid changes directly into a gas.
A gas changes directly into a solid.

en.text: A change of state changes the form of a substance, not what it is. Heating a solid melts it into a liquid. Cooling a liquid freezes it into a solid. Heating a liquid evaporates it into a gas. Cooling a gas condenses it into a liquid. Energy must be added or removed.

screens.title: Ice on a plate
screens.ask: An ice cube sits on a plate in a warm classroom. What happens?
screens.after: It melts. The warm room gives it energy, so the particles speed up and slide past each other.

screens.title: 2.1.6 Changes in state
paras: A change of state is a change from one physical form to another.
Melting, freezing, evaporation and condensation are changes of state.
The substance does not change; only its state changes.
To change a state, energy must be added or removed.

screens.title: Solids and liquids
paras: A warmed solid's particles gain energy and speed up. They slide past one another.
A solid changing into a liquid on heating is melting (fusion).
A cooled liquid's particles slow down and lock into a fixed pattern.
A liquid changing into a solid is freezing (solidification). This happens at the freezing point.

screens.title: Liquids and gases
paras: A warmed liquid's particles gain energy. Some escape from the surface as a gas.
A liquid changing into a gas is evaporation.
A cooled gas's particles lose energy and come together.
A gas changing into a liquid is condensation.
screens.note: Evaporation happens at the surface, even below the boiling point. Wet clothes dry this way. At the boiling point the liquid boils.

screens.title: Activity 2.5: name each arrow
screens.text: Solid —A→ Liquid —B→ Gas, and back: Gas —C→ Liquid —D→ Solid.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The change of a substance from one physical form to another.
A solid changes into a liquid on heating. Also called fusion.
A liquid changes into a solid. Also called solidification.
A liquid changes into a gas.
A gas changes into a liquid.

screens.text: Water droplets form on the outside of a cold bottle of water. What is this?
screens.why: Water vapour in the air cools on the bottle and becomes liquid.
These are the four arrows of Activity 2.5.
screens.clue: Melting is what ice does in the sun.

screens.text: When water freezes it becomes a different substance.
screens.why: Ice is still water. Only the state changes.
screens.clue: Can the ice melt back into water?

screens.text: When a liquid is warmed, its particles …
opts: gain energy and some escape as a gas
screens.ans: gain energy and some escape as a gas

screens.text: Wet clothes dry on a line in Adama, even though the air is far below 100 °C. Why?
opts: Water evaporates from the surface below its boiling point
screens.ans: Water evaporates from the surface below its boiling point
screens.why: Some surface particles gain enough energy to escape as a gas. This happens at any temperature, faster when warm.

en.text: Some substances change between solid and gas without becoming a liquid. Solid to gas directly is sublimation. Iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice sublime. Gas to solid directly is deposition.

screens.title: No puddle
screens.ask: Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) is left on a table. It gets smaller, but there is no puddle. Where did it go?
opts: It became a liquid and dried
It turned straight into a gas
screens.after: Dry ice changes straight from solid to gas. This is called sublimation.

screens.title: Solids and gases
paras: Some solids and gases change state without ever becoming a liquid.
The change from a solid directly into a gas is sublimation.
Iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice undergo sublimation.
Deposition is the change from a gas directly into a solid.

screens.text: Which of these is NOT the same process as the others?
screens.why: Freezing, solidification and crystallization all mean liquid → solid. Condensation is gas → liquid.
